Status

FinKore Core 2.0.3 stable.

Purpose

This document defines the normative portable JSON representation of Money. It specifies interchange only and does not constrain internal amount representation; see Money Representation.

Requirements

  • MONEY-SERIALIZATION-001 — Serialized Money MUST include amount and currency.
  • MONEY-SERIALIZATION-002 — amount MUST be a JSON string containing a base-10 decimal in plain notation: an optional minus sign, one or more integer digits, and an optional decimal point followed by one or more fractional digits.
  • MONEY-SERIALIZATION-003 — amount MUST NOT contain exponential notation, a leading plus sign, or non-finite tokens.
  • MONEY-SERIALIZATION-004 — currency MUST be a JSON string satisfying Currency.
  • MONEY-SERIALIZATION-005 — A parser MUST reject non-finite, malformed, or ambiguous amounts.
  • MONEY-SERIALIZATION-006 — Unknown members MAY be accepted by an implementation.
  • MONEY-SERIALIZATION-007 — Unknown members MUST NOT alter the meaning of amount or currency.
  • MONEY-SERIALIZATION-008 — Serialization followed by deserialization MUST preserve numeric amount and currency.

Invariants

Serialization followed by deserialization preserves numeric amount and currency as required by MONEY-SERIALIZATION-008.

Portable serialization does not assign financial meaning to lexical scale. "10", "10.0", and "10.00" are distinct valid JSON strings representing the same exact amount, and an implementation may emit any of them unless a separate presentation request applies. A consumer that needs a unique test or display spelling must apply an explicitly documented presentation normalization without changing the numeric amount. Such normalization is not rounding and is not a storage-scale requirement.

An optional native serialization scale is a presentation request, not an implicit rounding policy. Extending scale or removing only trailing zeros is consistent with MONEY-SERIALIZATION-008. Discarding a non-zero remainder is not: 1.239 EUR and -1.239 EUR cannot be serialized at scale 2 without changing value. Such requests fail with FINKORE_MONEY_ROUNDING_REQUIRED under MONEY-ROUNDING-006 and MONEY-ERROR-005. A caller can explicitly round first and serialize the resulting Money value. Failure preserves the original operand under MONEY-ERROR-007.

This does not require every language API to expose a scale argument or require preservation of lexical trailing zeros. The native scale-validation boundary uses the non-negative integer target-scale meaning in Rounding. A requested negative, non-integral, malformed, or unsupported scale fails with FINKORE_MONEY_INVALID_ROUNDING under MONEY-ERROR-006, before determining whether a valid scale would lose value. Boolean and string coercion cannot repair a malformed scale. Native APIs document their supported scale range and representation of no scale request; this introduces no universal upper bound and does not import Allocation's bounded scale profile into serialization.

Normative Examples

These examples use the normative member names and value encodings. They have the same Money meaning; neither spelling is preferred by this specification.

{
  "amount": "1299.90",
  "currency": "EUR"
}
{
  "amount": "1299.9",
  "currency": "EUR"
}

Invalid Examples

{ "amount": 1299.90, "currency": "EUR" }

The numeric JSON form is not portable because its host may apply binary floating-point semantics.

Errors

Malformed data fails as defined by MONEY-ERROR-001 or MONEY-ERROR-002 in Money Errors, as applicable.

Presentation scale

Portable serialization does not need to preserve presentation scale. This is an explicit reading of MONEY-REPRESENTATION-005 and MONEY-SERIALIZATION-008, not a new rounding permission. Removing or adding only insignificant zeros preserves value; discarding a non-zero digit still requires an explicit rounding rule. The conformance observation convention uses deterministic presentation for exact comparison without requiring one production spelling.
